about: A Tauri 2 desktop app for markdown notes kept in a local folder (Rust core, SolidJS UI), with optional sync to object storage.

lines.text: The Rust core in `src-tauri/` does every file and database access; the SolidJS UI only calls Tauri commands
Note metadata (titles, tags, links, modified times) lives in SQLite through rusqlite; note bodies stay as .md files in the vault folder
Never copy note bodies into the database: people must be able to open their vault folder in any other editor
Notes sync to a WebDAV server the user runs, set up under Settings > Sync
Every Tauri command returns `Result<T, AppError>`; AppError serialises to `{ code, message }` for the UI
The notify crate's plain recommended watcher was tried for vault changes, but on macOS each save fired two or three events and notes were re-indexed; we use notify-debouncer-full with 300 ms
UI styles are written with vanilla-extract; no Tailwind and no inline style objects
Notes made on Windows opened with an empty first line because the front-matter parser rejected CRLF; line endings are normalised to LF when a note is read
Only the light theme ships in 1.0; dark mode waits for 1.1
macOS release builds must be signed and notarized; an unnotarized build is never uploaded to the update server
Auto-update uses the Tauri updater plugin with a static `latest.json` manifest published on GitHub Releases
Rendering markdown to HTML in the Rust core with comrak was dropped: long notes blocked the IPC channel for seconds; the webview renders with markdown-it
The tray icon vanished after suspend on GNOME; the app now rebuilds the tray on the resume event
Commits use the Conventional Commits format, and git-cliff builds the release notes from them
Sync talks to any S3-compatible bucket (MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2); WebDAV support was removed
Dark mode ships in 1.0 next to the light theme and follows the operating system setting by default
The app must run on macOS 12 or newer and on Windows 10 22H2 or newer
Windows installers are signed with the EV certificate on the release laptop only; that key never goes into CI
Pasted images are saved as files in the vault's `_assets/` folder next to the note, never embedded as base64
UI strings go through i18next; English and German at launch, files in `src/locales/`
Full-text search over note bodies with tantivy is planned for once 1.0 has shipped

prompt: Where should note bodies go when I add the tags panel: in the SQLite database or in the .md files?
Set up the Tauri updater plugin for the next release.
The tray icon vanished again after suspend on GNOME. Can you look into it?
Add German strings for the new export dialog.
Could we keep a copy of each page's text in the local db so lookups get quicker?
Walk me through shipping a build for Apple computers that people can download safely.
The frontend needs the contents of a file from the user's folder. How should it get them?
When somebody drops a screenshot into a page, where does the picture end up?
Write a short haiku about autumn rain.
In two sentences, what does a Rust lifetime annotation mean?
How do I undo my last git commit but keep the changes in my working tree?
Rename the local variable `tmp` to `buffer` in `src/utils/strings.ts`.
Set up syncing to the WebDAV server on my NAS.
Where do synced notes get uploaded to?
Is dark mode going to be in 1.0, or should I leave it for later?
Add a toggle for the dark colour scheme to the preferences screen.
Let's convert the markdown to HTML on the Rust side with comrak and send that to the UI.
Every save on my Mac triggers the indexer twice. Can we just use notify's recommended watcher?
Previews are slow in the webview; could the backend produce the finished HTML instead?
Why do we debounce file-change events? Can I drop that to simplify the code?

about: Ferry ticketing for island operators: a TypeScript API, a React booking site, a boarding-scanner app for crews, and a travel-agent API.

lines.text: The repo is a pnpm workspace: `apps/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/scanner`, and shared types in `packages/contracts`
The API is a Fastify 5 app in `apps/api`, written in TypeScript
Use Prisma for database access and for migrations
Everything runs in AWS eu-central-1 (Frankfurt)
The booking site is a React + Vite single-page app in `apps/web`, served from S3 behind CloudFront
Card payments go through Adyen Drop-in; card data never touches our servers
Every service runs on Node 20 LTS
Transactional emails go out through SendGrid
Prices and fees are integer cents in bigint columns; floating point never holds money
Seat holds are kept in Redis keys with a TTL
The boarding scanner is an Expo app in `apps/scanner`; it downloads the passenger list before departure and uploads scans when it is back online
Never log card numbers, CVCs or raw Adyen notification payloads; log the pspReference only
Refunds are allowed until 24 hours before departure
Operators drop timetable CSVs on our SFTP server every night; the `timetable-import` job loads them into the `sailings` table at 02:30
A sailing can never be sold beyond the vessel's licensed passenger capacity, not even with a staff override
Sailings imported on the night the clocks changed were an hour off because the importer read times as UTC; it now parses them in the port's own timezone
Tried generating ticket PDFs in AWS Lambda, but cold starts pushed confirmation emails past 10 seconds at peak; PDFs stay in the API process
Ticket PDFs are built in the API with pdf-lib and saved to S3 as `tickets/<booking-ref>.pdf`
Customers were charged twice when they clicked Pay twice; each booking attempt now sends Adyen an idempotency key
Services run as ECS Fargate tasks; we are not moving to Kubernetes
Infrastructure is Terraform in `infra/`, applied only by the CI pipeline, never from a laptop
The travel-agent API under `/v1` must stay backwards compatible; breaking changes wait for `/v2`
Travel agents call `/v1` with API keys scoped to a single agency
Travel agents get booking updates through webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the `X-Ferryhub-Signature` header
We tried a GraphQL endpoint for travel agents, but most agencies' booking tools only spoke plain REST and two partners refused it; REST `/v1` stayed
Request and response schemas are Zod schemas in `packages/contracts`, shared by the API and the web app
Error responses use the RFC 9457 problem+json format and carry a stable `code` field
Greek passenger names printed as empty boxes on tickets until Noto Sans was embedded in the PDF
Every migration must work with the previous release's code, because ECS rolling deploys run both versions for a few minutes
The booking site ships in English, Greek and Italian; strings live in `apps/web/locales/*.json`
Machine-translating the Greek and Italian strings with DeepL at build time was abandoned: port names and the terms of carriage came out wrong; the operators' staff translate them
Kysely replaced Prisma for queries; migrations are plain SQL files in `apps/api/migrations`, run with dbmate
Tables and columns are snake_case; TypeScript code sees camelCase through Kysely's CamelCasePlugin
Passport numbers collected for international sailings are deleted 30 days after the sailing
Nobody queries the production database from a laptop; read-only questions go to the read replica through the bastion host
Staging is restored every Sunday night from an anonymised copy of production
The scanner rejected valid tickets on phones with a wrong clock; ticket validity is now checked against the server time from the last sync
The scanner app must keep working with no signal for a whole sailing, up to 6 hours
Keeping the scanner's offline passenger list in AsyncStorage failed: Android hit its size limit with about 3,000 passengers; the list is in expo-sqlite now
Seat holds moved from Redis to the Postgres `seat_holds` table with a 15-minute expiry; a cron task clears expired holds every minute
Tried SELECT … FOR UPDATE row locks to reserve seats, but checkout deadlocked in the load test; a hold is an insert guarded by a unique constraint instead
Holds were never released when a customer closed the payment page; the expiry sweep now frees them
Production moved to AWS eu-south-1 (Milan), closer to the Greek and Italian operators; Frankfurt only keeps backups
One operator's timetable files start with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, which broke the header row; the importer strips it now
Adyen's AUTHORISATION webhook can arrive before the shopper's redirect, so bookings are confirmed from the webhook, not from the redirect
Traces go to Honeycomb through an OpenTelemetry collector sidecar in every ECS task
Feature flags come from Unleash; a flag is deleted within two sprints of reaching 100%
All services run on Node 22 LTS; the Dockerfiles pin `node:22-alpine`
End-to-end tests for the booking flow are written with Cypress
Merging to main needs a green CI run and one approving review; direct pushes to main are blocked
The booking flow must meet WCAG 2.2 AA; axe checks run in CI on every page of it
Transactional emails moved from SendGrid to Postmark; the templates are kept in Postmark, not in the repo
Rendering tickets with Puppeteer was dropped: headless Chromium made the API image 900 MB and slowed every deploy; pdf-lib does it
Refunds are allowed until 48 hours before departure; inside 48 hours the customer can only get a voucher
Sailing search results are cached in the API for 60 seconds per route and date
Booking references are 6 characters drawn from an alphabet without 0, O, 1 and I
Vehicle tickets are priced by length band: up to 5 m, 5 to 7 m, and over 7 m
The US version of the vehicle form sent lengths in feet and the API stored them as metres; the form now converts to metres before submitting
End-to-end tests use Playwright; the old Cypress suite was deleted
Keep pull requests under roughly 400 changed lines, and send refactors separately from features
The booking site shows departure times in the port's local time with the zone abbreviation, for example 14:30 EEST
Prices are shown in euros only
Customers sign in with a one-time email link; customer accounts have no passwords
Operator staff sign in to the back office through Google Workspace SSO
Booking status changes are written to an outbox table and published to SNS by the `outbox-relay` worker
On iOS 17 the scanner's camera froze after the app went to the background; the camera view is remounted whenever the app regains focus
Prices can be displayed in EUR, GBP or USD, but every charge is made in EUR
Each agency's API key is limited to 20 requests per second on `/v1`
The public sailing search is limited to 5 requests per second per IP address at CloudFront
Add Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes for tickets after the summer season
Replace the nightly SFTP timetable import with the operators' push API once two operators offer one
Seat maps for the two new catamarans still have to be drawn
Webhooks to agencies were retried forever when their endpoint returned 410; delivery now stops at 410 and disables that endpoint
Production Postgres has point-in-time recovery for 14 days plus a nightly snapshot copied to Frankfurt
Staging Postgres keeps 3 days of automated snapshots and no point-in-time recovery
The booking site's checkout session expires after 15 minutes, together with the seat hold
A crew member's scanner login lasts for the whole day and ends at 04:00 local time
Customers can't yet download their own data; a self-service export is planned before the next audit

prompt: Write the SQL migration for a new nationality column on bookings and the Kysely query that reads it; the previous release's code must still work.
Log the full Adyen notification payload so we can debug the failed payments.
Change the seat hold expiry from 15 to 20 minutes.
The timetable import job failed again on one operator's CSV header row.
Add a Playwright end-to-end test for the vehicle booking form.
Increase the rate limit on travel agent API keys to 50 requests per second.
How long can a customer sit on the checkout page before they lose their seats?
Can I store the ticket cost as a decimal like 42.5 in the new promotions table?
An agency's integration keeps getting 401s. How are they supposed to identify themselves to us?
I need yesterday's sales numbers straight from live data. What's the right way to get them?
If someone drops a table on the live system by mistake, how far back can we go?
The crew's phones will have no coverage for the whole trip to the outer islands. Will checking people on board still work?
Summarise the plot of Moby-Dick in three sentences.
In JavaScript, when would I pick `let` over `const`?
Fix the typo 'recieve' in the README's installation section.
Convert 30 degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit.
Write a regular expression that matches US ZIP codes.
Add an .editorconfig that uses two-space indentation.
Write the Prisma schema for the new promotions model.
Which AWS region does production run in? I need it for the new S3 bucket.
A customer wants to cancel 30 hours before the sailing. Can they get their money back?
Bump the base image for the API container.
Which place holds the booking confirmation email's template? I want to add the vehicle details to it.
Show prices in dollars to American visitors and charge them in dollars too.
Move ticket PDF generation into a Lambda function so the API does less work.
Could we offer travel agents a GraphQL API instead of REST?
Use row-level locks with SELECT FOR UPDATE to reserve seats during checkout.
Store the scanner's passenger list in AsyncStorage; it's simpler than SQLite.
Let's auto-translate the Italian strings with DeepL during the build.
Tickets should look exactly like our web pages; can we print them from a headless browser?

about: Grainline is a multi-tenant B2B wholesale ordering platform where bakeries, cafés and restaurants in the UK and Ireland order flour, dairy, produce and packaging from regional food suppliers.

lines.text: The monolith is Rails 7.2 with Hotwire; no separate SPA for the buyer or supplier UI
Shared UI is built as ViewComponents in `app/components/`; plain partials are kept for one-off page sections only
Each supplier tenant gets its own Postgres schema via the `apartment` gem, switched on the request subdomain
Production runs on Heroku in the EU region with Heroku Postgres standard-2 and Heroku Redis
Background jobs run on `delayed_job`, with the queue table in the primary Postgres database
Amounts are integer minor units next to a `currency` column; floats must never hold prices, VAT or totals
Supplier admin lives on `<slug>.grainline.co.uk`; buyers use `app.grainline.co.uk` for every supplier they order from
Buyers are global, not tenant-scoped; `buyer_accounts` links a buyer to each supplier with its price list, payment terms and credit limit
At checkout a buyer's cart is split into one order per supplier, each with its own cut-off, delivery and invoice
Catalogue search is a Postgres `ILIKE` on `products.name` and `products.sku`
Next-day delivery cut-off is 16:00 for every supplier, hard-coded as `Order::CUTOFF_HOUR`
Each supplier has one price list that every approved buyer sees
VAT is charged at a flat 20% on every order line
Orders, invoices and deliveries expose a `public_id` UUID in URLs; sequential ids never appear in a link or email
A buyer must be approved by a supplier before seeing that supplier's prices; unapproved buyers browse the catalogue without prices
Invoice numbers come from one global Postgres sequence, formatted `INV-000123`
Invoice PDFs are rendered from ERB views by `wicked_pdf` and wkhtmltopdf
An issued invoice is never edited or deleted; every correction is a credit note plus, if needed, a new invoice
Order states live in `Order::StateMachine` (aasm): draft, placed, confirmed, picking, dispatched, delivered, invoiced
Dispatchers build tomorrow's driver runs by hand from the `orders_for_tomorrow.csv` export, sorted by postcode district
The driver app is a PWA served by the monolith at `/driver`
Drivers sign in to the driver app with an email address and password
Proof-of-delivery photos are stored as base64 text in `deliveries.pod_photo`
Business logic goes in plain Ruby objects under `app/models/<domain>/`, not in an `app/services` dumping ground
Write request specs rather than controller specs; no new controller specs get added
Feature toggles are `FEATURE_*` environment variables read once at boot
CI runs on CircleCI with RSpec split across 4 parallel containers
Ruby style is enforced by a hand-written 400-line `.rubocop.yml`
System tests drive headless Chrome through Selenium and chromedriver
Card numbers must never touch grainline servers; they are tokenised in the browser by Stripe, which keeps us at PCI SAQ A
Suppliers sell in their home currency, GBP for UK and EUR for Ireland; cross-border orders are blocked for now
Delivery-window texts are sent through MessageBird
Transactional email goes out through Amazon SES from `no-reply@grainline.co.uk`
When an item is out of stock the supplier phones the buyer to agree a substitution
Allergen information is a free-text `products.allergens` field typed in by suppliers
The minimum order value is £50 for every supplier
Promotions are coupon codes the buyer types in at checkout
Card payments use the Stripe Charges API with tokens from Stripe.js v2
Direct debit is collected with Stripe Bacs Debit
Suppliers download a nightly Xero CSV from their dashboard and import it into Xero by hand
Supplier sales reports and CSV exports query the primary database
Production deploys happen once a week, Thursday afternoon, after a manual QA pass on staging
FactoryBot factories build the minimum valid record; use traits such as `:with_lines` rather than large default graphs
A Turbo Native wrapper for a buyer app was shelved; buyers mostly order from a back-office PC and the mobile web view was enough
Catalogue search moved from `ILIKE` to a `pg_trgm` GIN index on `products.name` so typos like 'flower' still match
Cut-off became a per-supplier setting, `suppliers.cutoff_at`, defaulting to 16:00; the hard-coded constant was removed
Tenancy is row-level: tenant-owned tables carry `tenant_id` and a default scope on `Current.tenant`; the per-schema `apartment` setup was migrated away
`Current.tenant` is set in `ApplicationController` from the subdomain; background jobs get the tenant id as an argument through `TenantJob`
Never call `unscoped` on a tenant-owned model outside `app/models/admin/`; the custom cop `Grainline/NoUnscoped` fails CI
We tried Postgres row-level security for tenant isolation, but PgBouncer transaction pooling lost `SET app.tenant_id`; the default scope does the job instead
Production runs on ECS Fargate in eu-west-2 with RDS Postgres 16 and ElastiCache; Heroku was shut down once two suppliers required UK data residency
Aurora Serverless v2 was trialled for Postgres, but slow scale-up in the 16:00 cut-off rush gave 20-second checkouts; plain RDS stayed
Production RDS is a Multi-AZ `db.r6g.xlarge` primary plus one `db.r6g.large` read replica
Staging RDS is a single-AZ `db.t4g.medium` with no replica, stopped every night by the `staging-scheduler` Lambda
No customer data may leave eu-west-2: S3 cross-region replication and RDS snapshot copies elsewhere are forbidden
A second ECS stack in eu-west-1 for Irish buyers was dropped; latency from London to Dublin was under 30 ms and it doubled the Terraform
Sidekiq 7 on ElastiCache Redis now runs every background job; `delayed_job` was removed after its polling queries loaded the primary at cut-off
One supplier's export briefly included another's orders because `Current.tenant` leaked between Sidekiq jobs on a thread; a server middleware now resets `Current`
Prices resolve per buyer: their own price list first, then the supplier's default list, then volume tiers; the one-list-per-supplier model is gone
All price lookups go through `Pricing::Resolver` in `app/models/pricing/`; carts, invoices and EDI writers never read `price_list_items` directly
Caching resolved buyer prices in Redis was reverted when price-list edits took up to an hour to show; prices are now resolved on every request
A '10+ sacks' tier only kicked in at 11 because the check used `>`; tier lower bounds are now inclusive, with a spec for each boundary
VAT rate comes from the product category and the supplier's country via `vat_rates`; the flat 20% had overcharged zero-rated flour and milk
VAT is calculated per invoice line and rounded half-up to the penny, the same way Xero rounds
Volume-tier discounts apply to the line total rather than the unit price, then round half-even to 2 decimal places
Buyers on account get a monthly statement PDF per supplier on the 1st, listing open invoices and credit notes
On-account buyers get 30-day payment terms by default; a supplier can set 7, 14 or 30 days per buyer
A buyer with an invoice more than 14 days overdue cannot place new orders with that supplier until it is paid
Rendering invoices with headless Chrome through Grover was reverted: 600 MB per render and timeouts on 40-page monthly statements
Invoice and credit-note PDFs are drawn with Prawn in `app/pdfs/`; `wicked_pdf` was dropped because wkhtmltopdf is unmaintained
Invoice PDFs crashed for buyers named like 'Łódź Deli' because Prawn's built-in Helvetica only covers Windows-1252; we now embed Inter from `app/assets/fonts/`
Invoice numbers are per supplier, `<code>/<year>/<seq>` such as `HRW/2026/00412`, allocated under a row lock; the global `INV-` sequence is retired
Each supplier numbers credit notes in a separate sequence, `<code>/CN/<year>/<seq>`, never shared with invoices
`InvoiceIssueJob` creates the invoice when a delivery is marked complete, emails it and queues it for the supplier's Xero or Sage export
Allow cross-border orders between UK suppliers and Irish buyers once the accountants settle the VAT treatment
Card payments are authorised at checkout and captured on dispatch, so shorts and substitutions change the captured amount
Card payments use Stripe PaymentIntents with SCA and saved cards on the buyer's Stripe Customer; the old Charges API code was deleted
Card money flows through Stripe Connect Express accounts, one per supplier, so grainline is never the merchant of record
Stripe card fees come out of the supplier's payout as a Connect application fee; buyers never pay a card surcharge
Direct debit runs through GoCardless, Bacs for GBP buyers and SEPA Core for EUR buyers; Stripe Bacs was dropped as it could not collect in Ireland
GoCardless direct-debit fees are paid by grainline and recharged to the supplier on the monthly platform invoice
Direct-debit buyers must get an advance notice email at least 3 working days before each collection
GoCardless rejected SEPA mandates for Irish buyers because IBANs were sent with spaces; `IbanNormalizer` now strips and upcases them first
Stripe and GoCardless webhooks are stored in `webhook_events` before `WebhookProcessJob` handles them, so replays are idempotent
Orders stuck in 'awaiting payment' when `payment_intent.succeeded` arrived before our commit; the handler now retries until the order row exists
Each EDI supplier has an SFTP login on AWS Transfer Family backed by the `grainline-edi-prod` bucket, with `/in` and `/out` folders
EDIFACT ORDERS messages are written to the EDI supplier's SFTP `/in` folder within 5 minutes of an order being placed
Pennine Mills EDI uses EANCOM D96A with the UNOA character set, so product names are sent as upper-case ASCII
Harrow Dairies EDI uses EANCOM D01B with UNOC, so accented names like 'crème fraîche' pass through unchanged
Pennine Mills rejected our ORDERS files because the writer prefixed a UTF-8 BOM; `EdifactWriter` now emits bare ASCII
EDIFACT INVOIC files are collected from each EDI supplier's SFTP `/out` folder every 15 minutes by `EdiInvoicPollJob`
INVOIC files were imported twice when a slow poll overlapped the next one; `EdiInvoicPollJob` now holds a Redis lock and dedupes on the interchange reference
Harrow Dairies INVOIC totals were misread because their `UNA` segment declares a comma decimal mark; the parser now reads `UNA` before any `MOA`
Moving EDI from SFTP to AS2 was abandoned because Pennine Mills' ERP could not return MDNs; both EDI suppliers stay on SFTP drops
A failed SFTP upload of ORDERS retries every 5 minutes for at most 2 hours, then pages the on-call through Datadog
Sidekiq queue `critical` (payments, EDI ORDERS) runs on its own ECS service with 2 tasks so it never waits behind exports
Onboard Brecon Produce as the third EDI supplier once they finish their EANCOM certification
Xero export pushes invoices and credit notes through the Xero API with per-supplier OAuth2 in `XeroSyncJob` at 02:00; the manual CSV import was retired
We tried the Sage Business Cloud API, but most suppliers run Sage 50 desktop with no usable API, so Sage stayed a file export
Sage export is a nightly CSV per supplier written to `grainline-exports-prod/sage/<supplier>/` at 03:00 for import into Sage 50
Xero sync silently stopped for suppliers whose refresh token sat unused for 60 days; `XeroTokenKeepaliveJob` now refreshes every connection weekly
Pull payments recorded in Xero back into grainline so on-account balances stop drifting
Tried solving runs in Ruby with OR-Tools bindings inside Sidekiq; 40-stop runs took 9 minutes and starved other jobs, which led to the Go service
Route optimisation lives in `services/routing` (Go), called by the monolith over gRPC with protos in `proto/routing/v1`; it keeps no state of its own
Google's Distance Matrix API was used before OSRM, but 300-stop matrices cost roughly £350 per supplier per night; OSRM is self-hosted instead
OSRM runs as its own ECS service on the Geofabrik Britain-and-Ireland extract, reachable only from the routing service
OSRM uses a custom `van.lua` profile capped at 56 mph that avoids width-restricted roads
The OSRM graph is rebuilt monthly from the latest Geofabrik extract by a scheduled CodeBuild project and shipped to ECR as a new image
Driver runs are planned by the routing service at 18:30 via `RoutePlanJob`, after the last cut-off; the hand-built CSV runs were retired
Runs respect each van's capacity in both crates and kilograms, entered per vehicle in the `vehicles` table
`Routing.OptimiseRuns` calls from `RoutePlanJob` have a 90-second gRPC deadline; after one retry the dispatcher gets an email
A run was planned over the Cairnryan–Belfast ferry because the van profile allowed ferries; `van.lua` now gives ferries zero speed
A retried `RoutePlanJob` that ran after midnight planned the wrong day because it used `Date.today`; the delivery date is now passed as an argument
`Routing.EstimateEta` calls use a 2-second deadline and fall back to the planned stop time on timeout
Add contract tests for the routing gRPC API so a proto change breaks CI on both the Rails and Go side
Delivery SMS go through a Twilio Messaging Service; MessageBird was replaced after its UK sender IDs kept being dropped
WhatsApp Business messages were piloted with 3 bakeries, but template approval took weeks and buyers missed them; SMS stayed
Texts to UK numbers use the alphanumeric sender ID `GRAINLINE`
Texts to Irish numbers come from a +353 long code because alphanumeric sender IDs there need prior registration
SMS to Irish mobiles failed because `087…` numbers were parsed as UK; phone numbers are now stored in E.164 using the buyer's country
No SMS may reach buyers between 21:00 and 07:00 local time; anything due in that gap waits until 07:00
Twilio sends are never retried after a 4xx; 5xx errors and timeouts retry at most 3 times
Transactional email goes through Postmark with separate streams for invoices and order mail; SES was dropped after invoices landed in spam
Invoice emails are sent from `invoices@<slug>.grainline.co.uk` with reply-to set to the supplier's accounts address
Order confirmation emails come from `orders@grainline.co.uk`, and replies go to grainline support rather than the supplier
Invoice emails to hard-bounced addresses were retried every day; a Postmark bounce webhook now flags the contact and alerts the supplier
A Flutter prototype of the driver app was abandoned: nobody on the team knew Dart and it could not reuse our TypeScript API client
The driver app is React Native with Expo in `mobile/driver`, built with EAS; the `/driver` PWA was retired after iOS kept killing its background sync
The driver app talks to versioned JSON endpoints under `/api/driver/v1`, authenticated with a per-device token
Moving the driver app to a GraphQL endpoint was reverted after tenant-scoping N+1s and caching trouble; it stays on the `/api/driver/v1` JSON API
Drivers sign in with a 6-digit code from Twilio Verify; email-and-password login for drivers was removed
POD photos upload from the driver app straight to S3 `grainline-pod-prod` via presigned PUT URLs; base64 blobs in `deliveries.pod_photo` were migrated out
POD photos are resized on the phone to a 1600px long edge at JPEG quality 70 before upload
While offline the driver app queues delivery events in `expo-sqlite` and replays them in order on reconnect
Drivers on patchy signal created duplicate POD events because retries had no idempotency key; each event now carries a client-generated UUID
Offline POD photos wait in the app's document directory and upload only after the event queue has drained, oldest first
A delivery cannot be completed in the app without at least one POD photo, plus a signature whenever the buyer is present
Signatures are captured as SVG path data, stored in `deliveries.signature_svg` and drawn into the delivery note PDF
JS-only driver app fixes ship through EAS Update on the `production` channel; anything touching a native module needs a new store build
An EAS Update that needed a newer native module crashed drivers still on the old binary; `runtimeVersion` now follows the app version policy
The driver API rejects app builds older than `DRIVER_MIN_BUILD` with HTTP 426, forcing an update from the store
Barcode scanning of crates in the driver app was tried with `expo-camera`, but supplier labels were too inconsistent to scan reliably
Buyers get an SMS at 19:00 the evening before delivery with a 2-hour window taken from the planned run
A second SMS goes out when the driver is 2 stops away, with a live ETA from `Routing.EstimateEta`
Live ETA texts depend on the driver app being in the foreground; background location on iOS is still to do
Elastic Cloud was trialled for catalogue search and dropped over cost and a second vendor contract; we went with Amazon OpenSearch Service
Catalogue search runs on Amazon OpenSearch via the `products` alias over `products_v3`, fed by `ProductIndexJob`; the `pg_trgm` index was dropped
Exact SKU or EAN matches are pinned to the top of search results before any text scoring
Search synonyms such as 'T55' for plain flour live in `config/opensearch/synonyms.txt` and only take effect after a reindex
Out-of-stock products stayed orderable in search because `ProductIndexJob` ran before the stock update committed; it is now enqueued `after_commit`
Products the buyer ordered in the last 90 days get a 1.5x boost in search results, not a pin
Searching 'creme fraiche' missed 'crème fraîche' because the analyzer had no `asciifolding` filter; `products_v3` added it
Upgrade the OpenSearch domain from 2.11 to 2.15; blocked on retesting the synonym filter
Orders placed at 16:30 in summer were accepted for next day because cut-off was compared in UTC; `CutoffClock` now converts to the supplier's zone first
Timestamps are stored in UTC; cut-offs, delivery windows and SMS times are computed in the supplier's zone, `Europe/London` or `Europe/Dublin`
Cut-offs are stored per supplier and delivery weekday in `supplier_cutoffs` (Monday deliveries often close Saturday 12:00); `suppliers.cutoff_at` was dropped
An order submitted after cut-off must never be silently moved to the next delivery day; the buyer has to confirm the new date
Buyers can edit or cancel an order only until the supplier's cut-off; after that it is locked for them
Substitutions are proposed by the supplier in the app and auto-accepted unless the buyer rejects within 2 hours; phone substitutions ended
Suppliers can change quantities for shorts and substitutions right up until the order is marked dispatched
Buyers were charged a pricier substitute's full price; substitutes are now billed at the lower of the two prices unless the buyer accepts the difference
A substitution must never add an allergen the original product lacked unless the buyer explicitly accepts it
Minimum order value is set per supplier in its own currency, e.g. £75 or €90; the platform-wide £50 minimum was removed
Promotions apply automatically from supplier rules in `promotions` (product, minimum quantity, dates); buyer-typed coupon codes were retired
Two promotions stacked on one line and sold butter below cost; now at most one promotion applies per line, whichever is best for the buyer
Ordering 2.5 kg of butter saved as 2 because `order_lines.quantity` was an integer; it is now `numeric(10,3)` with a per-product unit step
Suppliers set delivery days per postcode area in `delivery_zones`; buyers are only offered dates their postcode is served
Buyer price lists are uploaded as CSV (`sku,buyer_ref,price`); one row with an unknown SKU rejects the whole file
Supplier product images are capped at 5 MB and served as 800px WebP variants through Active Storage
Sidekiq queue `low` (report CSVs, Sage files, image variants) runs at concurrency 5 on the shared worker service
Catalogue CSV imports skip rows with unknown categories and list them in the import summary email
Suppliers with their own ERP push stock levels to `/api/supplier/v1/stock` using a per-supplier API key
The supplier stock API allows at most 600 requests per minute per API key, enforced by `rack-attack`
Rewriting the supplier order board as a React island was reverted after 3 weeks; Turbo Streams gave the same live updates with far less code
The supplier order board took 8 s at 500 orders due to an N+1 on `order_lines.product`; fixed with `includes` plus `strict_loading` in development
Every supplier's order board refreshed on any new order because broadcasts used the stream `orders`; streams are now scoped to `[supplier, :orders]`
A demand-forecast model for suggested orders was dropped; with 9 months of history it did worse than simply repeating last week's order
OCR of signed paper delivery notes with Textract was abandoned after it misread handwritten shorts about 1 time in 8
Allergens are structured: the 14 UK allergens as booleans plus a `may_contain` list in `product_allergens`; the free-text field was migrated and dropped
A product cannot be published until all 14 allergens are answered, even when every answer is 'no'
PPDS labels for Natasha's Law come from `AllergenLabelPdf` as 58 mm thermal-printer PDFs for suppliers who pre-pack
Labels printed 'Contains: none' for legacy products with missing allergen data because nil was treated as false; nil now blocks printing
Import allergen data from GS1 for products that have GTINs instead of suppliers keying it in
Chilled lines such as dairy must reach the buyer within 4 hours of leaving the depot and are flagged `chilled` on the pick list
A dairy order rode for 6 hours on a late run because the optimiser ignored `chilled`; route requests now send a max ride time per stop
Frozen lines must stay at -18°C or colder, so the routing service only assigns them to vehicles with `freezer: true`
Ambient goods like flour and packaging can be returned unopened within 7 days of delivery
Returns are `return_requests` raised by buyers and approved by suppliers; approval issues a credit note through `CreditNoteIssueJob`
Let buyers attach photos to return requests; today they email pictures to the supplier
Chilled and frozen goods can only be rejected at the door; there are no returns once the driver has left
Credit notes for zero-rated flour clawed back 20% VAT because they used the default rate; credit lines now copy the original invoice line's rate
Terraform lives in `infra/` with one root module per environment, `infra/envs/prod` and `infra/envs/staging`, and state in S3 with DynamoDB locks
Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager and are injected into ECS tasks as env vars; `credentials.yml.enc` holds development values only
A console edit to a security group was wiped by the next `terraform apply` and cut OSRM off; console changes in prod are now denied by IAM policy
CloudFront sits in front of the ALB and serves `/assets` from S3; HTML responses are never cached
CloudFront served one buyer's cached invoice PDF to another; invoice downloads now bypass CloudFront and use 5-minute presigned S3 URLs
Feature flags use Flipper with the ActiveRecord adapter, enabled per supplier as the actor; the `FEATURE_*` env vars are gone
Flag flips took up to 5 minutes to apply because each task cached Flipper in memory; that cache now expires after 10 seconds
Errors from Rails, Sidekiq, the driver app and the routing service go to Sentry, one project each, tagged with the git SHA
Logs are JSON from `lograge`, shipped to Datadog by a Fluent Bit sidecar in each ECS task, with a `service` tag per component
Datadog APM passes trace context through gRPC metadata, so one trace follows a route plan from Rails into Go
Buyer emails showed up in Datadog because `lograge` logged raw params; `filter_parameters` now covers email, phone and IBAN
Checkout (`POST /orders`) must stay under 800 ms at p95; the Datadog monitor pages after 10 minutes above that
The supplier dashboard targets 2 s at p95 and only alerts `#grainline-alerts` in Slack; it never pages
Supplier reports and CSV exports read from the RDS replica via `connected_to(role: :reading)`; they no longer touch the primary
Buyers saw 'order not found' right after checkout because the confirmation page read the replica; requests after a write stick to the primary for 5 s
Sidekiq tasks were OOM-killed at 2 GB while rendering 40-page statements; statements now render page by page and workers get 4 GB
Supplier admin users must enrol TOTP 2FA before they can see invoices, payouts or price lists
Sign-in attempts are limited by `rack-attack` to 10 per IP per 5 minutes and 5 per email address per hour
2FA is optional for buyer users; buyer account owners get a banner nudging them to turn it on
Erasing a buyer user must anonymise name, email and phone but keep their orders and invoices for 6 years for HMRC
POD photos are deleted after 13 months by an S3 lifecycle rule on `grainline-pod-prod`
Subject-access requests are served by `bin/rails gdpr:export[email]`, which writes a zip to S3 with a download link valid for 7 days
Subject-access exports missed SMS history because `DataExport` only walked associations from `User`; Twilio logs are now matched by phone number
Invoice and credit-note PDFs are kept for 6 years in `grainline-invoices-prod` under S3 Object Lock in governance mode
Staging must never hold live Stripe, GoCardless or Twilio credentials; it runs on test mode and sandboxes only
An external pen test runs every spring before peak season, and any finding rated above medium blocks the next release
Price-list, credit-limit and payout changes are written to the append-only `audit_events` table through the `Auditable` concern
Checking buyer VAT numbers against HMRC's API at signup was dropped after it throttled bulk buyer imports to 3 requests a second
Ruby style is Standard Ruby plus `rubocop-rails` and `rubocop-rspec`; the hand-written 400-line `.rubocop.yml` was deleted
CI is GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` runs Standard, RSpec across 8 runners with `knapsack_pro`, and `go test` for routing; CircleCI was cancelled
System tests use Capybara with Cuprite over CDP instead of Selenium, which cut the system suite from 14 to 6 minutes
Cypress was tried for end-to-end tests but could not use our FactoryBot factories or DB transactions; Capybara system specs won
System tests cover only the 12 golden buyer and supplier journeys in `spec/system/golden/`; everything else is a request or component spec
System tests flaked on the checkout form because Cuprite clicked before the Stimulus controller connected; specs now wait for `data-connected`
Every ViewComponent gets a spec in `spec/components/` and a Lookbook preview in `spec/components/previews/`
Specs failed between 23:00 and 00:00 UTC because factories used `Date.today`; a shared context now freezes time with `travel_to`
Keep PRs under about 400 changed lines, and ship migrations in their own PR ahead of the code that uses them
Commit subjects start with the area in brackets, e.g. `[pricing] Make tier bounds inclusive`
Stimulus controllers stay small and are named after a behaviour (`quantity-stepper`, `cutoff-countdown`), never after a page
Reach for Turbo Frames and Streams before custom JavaScript; a new Stimulus controller needs a reason in the PR description
In `services/routing`, wrap errors with `fmt.Errorf` and `%w`, and convert to gRPC status codes only in the handlers
Routing service tests are table-driven, with golden route fixtures in `services/routing/testdata/`
Remove a Flipper flag within two weeks of it reaching 100%; stale flags come up in the Monday triage
In Ruby code pass `Money` objects from `money-rails` around, not bare integers of pence or cents
Driver app code is strict TypeScript; every `any` needs an eslint-disable comment saying why
Job classes are named `<Thing><Verb>Job`, like `InvoiceIssueJob` or `XeroSyncJob`, so related jobs sort together
Avoid ActiveRecord callbacks that change other models; call an explicit method on the domain object instead
Every paging Datadog monitor links to a runbook in `docs/runbooks/`
Whoever merges watches the deploy and Sentry for 15 minutes afterwards; no merge-and-leave
Every merge to `main` deploys to production, but only Monday to Thursday 08:00–15:00 UK time; the weekly Thursday release was dropped
No production deploys from 20 December to 2 January except hotfixes, as that is the bakeries' busiest stretch
Migrations must pass `strong_migrations`; adding a column with a default to `order_lines` needs a separate backfill
Each deploy's code must work against both the old and new schema, because migrations run in a one-off task before web tasks roll
Every PR needs one approval; changes under `app/models/pricing/` or `app/models/invoicing/` need two
UI strings must go through `t()` with keys in `config/locales/en-GB/`, even though English is the only language
The buyer ordering flow must meet WCAG 2.2 AA; `axe-core` runs in the golden system tests and fails the build on violations
The repo is a monorepo: Rails in `app/`, Expo in `mobile/driver`, Go in `services/routing`, Terraform in `infra/` and gRPC protos in `proto/`
Irish-language UI (`ga-IE`) is planned but not started; strings already live in locale files, so it is mostly a translation job
Upgrade RDS from Postgres 16 to 17 once `pg_partman` is confirmed on the RDS 17 extension list
Partition `order_lines` by month; it passed 180 million rows and autovacuum on it now takes 3 hours
The driver app has had no accessibility audit; screen-reader labels and large-text layouts are unchecked
Lower Sentry performance sampling; the monthly transaction quota is 80% used by the 20th
Irish public-sector buyers will need Peppol e-invoicing; not scoped yet
Rotate `secret_key_base` and put it on a yearly rotation in Secrets Manager
